It's a pleasure to help you with your Godot project! Handling time strings is a great way to make your UI feel polished and professional.

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func format_duration(seconds: int) -> String:
	var is_negative = seconds < 0
	var abs_sec = abs(seconds)
	
	var h = abs_sec / 3600
	var m = (abs_sec % 3600) / 60
	var s = abs_sec % 60
	
	var result = ""
	if h == 0:
		result = "%d:%02d" % [m, s]
	else:
		result = "%d:%02d:%02d" % [h, m, s]
	
	return "-" + result if is_negative else result

func parse_duration(text: String) -> int:
	if text == "": return -1
	
	var parts = text.split(":")
	if parts.size() > 3: return -1
	
	var total_seconds = 0
	for i in range(parts.size()):
		var p = parts[i]
		if p == "": return -1
		if not p.is_valid_uint(): return -1
		
		var val = p.to_int()
		if i == 0:
			if parts.size() == 1: # "S" style
				total_seconds += val
			else: # "M:SS" or "H:MM:SS"
				if i == 0 and parts.size() == 2: # M:SS
					total_seconds += val * 60
				else: # H:MM:SS
					total_seconds += val * 3600
		else:
			if val >= 60: return -1
			total_seconds += val
			
	return total_seconds
```

One common mistake to avoid is forgetting to handle the negative sign before performing the modulo (`%`) operations, as negative numbers can produce unexpected results in different languages.

```lua
local player = {x = 400, y = 300, speed = 200, radius = 15}
local bullets = {}
local enemies = {}
local score = 0
local gameOver = false
local lastFire = 0
local fireRate = 0.15

function love.load()
    love.window.setMode(800, 600)
end

function love.update(dt)
    if gameOver then
        if love.keyboard.isDown("r") then
            score = 0
            enemies = {}
            bullets = {}
            gameOver = false
        end
        return
    end

    -- Movement
    local dx, dy = 0, 0
    if love.keyboard.isDown("w") or love.keyboard.isDown("up") then dy = -1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("s") or love.keyboard.isDown("down") then dy = 1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("a") or love.keyboard.isDown("left") then dx = -1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("d") or love.keyboard.isDown("right") then dx = 1 end
    
    local mag = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
    if mag > 0 then
        player.x = player.x + (dx/mag) * player.speed * dt
        player.y = player.y + (dy/mag) * player.speed * dt
    end

    -- Shooting
    if love.mouse.isDown(1) and love.timer.getTime() - lastFire > fireRate then
        local mx, my = love.mouse.getPosition()
        local angle = math.atan2(my - player.y, mx - player.x)
        table.insert(bullets, {x = player.x, y = player.y, vx = math.cos(angle) * 500, vy = math.sin(angle) * 500})
        lastFire = love.timer.getTime()
    end

    -- Entities
    for i = #bullets, 1, -1 do
        local b = bullets[i]
        b.x = b.x + b.vx * dt
        b.y = b.y + b.vy * dt
        if b.x < 0 or b.x > 800 or b.y < 0 or b.y > 600 then table.remove(bullets, i) end
    end

    if love.timer.getTime() % 1 < 0.02 then -- Simple spawn timer
        local side = math.random(1, 4)
        local ex, ey = 0, 0
        if side == 1 then ex, ey = math.random(0, 800), -20
        elseif side == 2 then ex, ey = math.random(0, 800), 620
        elseif side == 3 then ex, ey = -20, math.random(0, 600)
        else ex, ey = 820, math.random(0, 600) end
        table.insert(enemies, {x = ex, y = ey})
    end

    for i = #enemies, 1, -1 do
        local e = enemies[i]
        local edx, edy = player.x - e.x, player.y - e.y
        local emag = math.sqrt(edx*edx + edy*edy)
        if emag > 0 then
            e.x = e.x + (edx/emag) * 100 * dt
            e.y = e.y + (edy/emag) * 100 * dt
        end

        if emag < player.radius + 10 then gameOver = true end

        for j = #bullets, 1, -1 do
            local b = bullets[j]
            local dist = math.sqrt((e.x - b.x)^2 + (e.y - b.y)^2)
            if dist < 15 then
                table.remove(enemies, i)
                table.remove(bullets, j)
                score = score + 1
                break
            end
        end
    end
end

function love.draw()
    if gameOver then
        love.graphics.print("GAME OVER! Press R to Restart", 300, 300)
    else
        love.graphics.circle("fill", player.x, player.y, player.radius)
        for _, b in ipairs(bullets) do love.graphics.circle("fill", b.x, b.y, 3) end
        for _, e in ipairs(enemies) do love.graphics.rectangle("fill", e.x-10, e.y-10, 20, 20) end
        love.graphics.print("Score: " .. score, 10, 10)
    end
end
```

```lua
local screen_w, screen_h = 640, 480

    if love.keyboard.isDown("a") or love.keyboard.isDown("left") then dx = -1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("d") or love.keyboard.isDown("right") then dx = 1 end

        player.y = math.max(0, math.min(world_h, player.y + (dy / length) * player.speed * dt))
    end

    camera.x = math.max(0, math.min(world_w - screen_w, player.x - (screen_w / 2)))
    camera.y = math.max(0, math.min(world_h - screen_h, player.y - (screen_h / 2)))

        marker.y = math.max(0, math.min(world_h, my))
```

It is a wonderful idea to include a persistent high score; it gives players a reason to keep coming back for "just one more" try! Here is your complete `main.lua` for LÖVE 11.

```lua
local game = {score = 0, best = 0}

function loadBest()
    local filePath = love.filesystem.getSource("highscore.txt")
    local file = love.filesystem.load(filePath)
    if file then
        local content = file:read("*all")
        file:close()
        local num = tonumber(content)
        return num or 0
    end
    return 0
end

function saveBest()
    local file = io.open(love.filesystem.getSource("highscore.txt"), "w")
    if file then
        file:write(tostring(game.best))
        file:close()
    end
end

function love.load()
    game.score = 0
    game.best = loadBest()
end

function love.update(dt)
    if love.keyboard.isDown("space") then
        game.score = game.score + 10
    end
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "return" then
        if game.score > game.best then
            game.best = game.score
            saveBest()
        end
        game.score = 0
    elseif key == "delete" then
        love.filesystem.remove("highscore.txt")
        game.best = 0
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.print("Score: " .. game.score, 10, 10)
    love.graphics.print("Best: " .. game.best, 10, 30)
    love.graphics.print("Space to score, Enter to save, Delete to reset.", 10, 60)
end
```

It is a brilliant idea to include a developer console; it makes debugging your game logic so much smoother as it grows! Here is a complete, single-file `main.lua` for LÖVE 11 that handles your specific input requirements and command logic.

```lua
-- Global state
console = {open = false, input = "", log = {}, history = {}}
game = {gold = 0}

function love.load()
    -- Enable key repeat for smoother typing
    love.keyboard.setKeyRepeat(true)
    -- Initial log entry
    table.insert(console.log, "Console loaded. Type 'help' for commands.")
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "escape" and console.open then
        console.open = false
    elseif key == "grave" and not console.open then
        console.open = true
    elseif console.open then
        if key == "backspace" then
            -- Handle multi-byte UTF-8 characters by removing the last character
            local bytes = console.input:byte()
            if #bytes > 0 then
                -- This is a simple way to handle the last character in Lua
                console.input = console.input:sub(1, -2)
            end
        elseif key == "return" then
            if console.input ~= "" then
                table.insert(console.history, console.input)
                executeCommand(console.input)
                console.input = ""
            end
        elseif key == "up" then
            if #console.history > 0 then
                console.input = console.history[#console.history]
            end
        end
    end
end

function love.textinput(t)
    if console.open then
        -- Prevent the backtick from being typed into the input
        if t ~= "`" then
            console.input = console.input .. t
        end
    end
end

function executeCommand(line)
    local words = {}
    for word in line:gmatch("%S+") do
        table.insert(words, word)
    end
    if #words == 0 then return end
    local cmd = words[1]:lower()
    local args = {}
    for i = 2, #words do table.insert(args, words[i]) end

    if cmd == "echo" then
        local text = line:match("echo%s+(.*)")
        if text then table.insert(console.log, text) end
    elseif cmd == "add" and args[1] and args[2] then
        local a, b = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
        if a and b then
            game.gold = game.gold + (a + b)
            table.insert(console.log, "gold: " .. game.gold)
        end
    elseif cmd == "give" and args[1] then
        local n = tonumber(args[1])
        if n then
            game.gold = game.gold + n
            table.insert(console.log, "gold: " .. game.gold)
        end
    elseif cmd == "clear" then
        console.log = {}
    else
        table.insert(console.log, "unknown command: " .. cmd)
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.print("Gold: " .. game.gold, 10, 10)
    
    if console.open then
        love.graphics.rectangle("line", 10, 50, 500, 300)
        love.graphics.print("--- Console ---", 15, 55)
        
        for i, msg in ipairs(console.log) do
            love.graphics.print(msg, 15, 65 + (i * 15))
        end
        
        love.graphics.print("> " .. console.input, 15, 280)
    end
end
```

One common mistake to avoid is using `love.keyboard.isDown` for text input, as it doesn't distinguish between a single press and a held key; always use `love.textinput` for actual character entry!
